examples.ko: 이 글은 기승전결이 분명해서 읽기 쉬워요.
examples.en: This piece has a clear structure, so it's easy to read.

examples.ko: 소설을 쓸 때 기승전결을 먼저 생각해 보세요.
examples.en: When you write a novel, think about the structure first.

examples.ko: 제 발표는 기승전결 없이 끝나 버렸어요.
examples.en: My presentation just ended without any real structure.
This drama follows the standard structure, so it's predictable.
In writing class, we also learn the four-part structure.

examples.ko: 사 컷 만화는 기승전결로 이야기를 풀어 가요.
examples.en: A four-panel comic tells its story in four parts.

explain: 글뿐 아니라 영화, 발표, 하루 일정처럼 이야기의 흐름을 말할 때도 써요. '기승전결이 뚜렷하다/없다'처럼 말하면 짜임새가 있는지를 평가하는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is used not only for writing but also for the flow of movies, presentations and even a day's schedule. Saying '기승전결이 뚜렷하다/없다' (the structure is clear / missing) judges whether something is well organized.

examples.ko: 음악 시간에 기악곡 감상 수업을 했어요.
examples.en: We had a lesson on listening to instrumental music in music class.
This instrumental piece is played on piano and violin.

examples.ko: 노래 없는 기악곡이 공부할 때 더 좋아요.
examples.en: Instrumental music without singing is better when I study.

examples.ko: 저는 성악곡보다 기악곡을 더 자주 들어요.
examples.en: I listen to instrumental pieces more often than vocal pieces.
I heard that only instrumental pieces are judged in this contest.
That composer is famous for instrumental works.

explain: '성악곡'의 반대말이라서 두 말을 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. 일상 대화에서는 '연주곡'이라고 쉽게 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the opposite of '성악곡' (vocal piece), so it helps to remember the two as a pair. In everyday talk people also say '연주곡' more simply.

examples.en: Seoraksan has so many strangely shaped rocks.
A small waterfall flows down between the oddly shaped rocks.
The tourists took photos with the strange rocks in the background.
This park is famous for its magnificent rock formations.
I kept marveling at the rock formations all the way up the trail.

examples.ko: 그 섬은 기암괴석과 푸른 바다가 어우러져 있어요.
examples.en: That island combines bizarre rocks with the blue sea.

explain: 산이나 바닷가의 특이하게 생긴 큰 바위를 감탄하며 말할 때 써요. 여행 소개글이나 기행문 같은 글말 느낌이라서 친구와 말할 때는 '신기하게 생긴 바위'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: You use it with admiration for oddly shaped big rocks on mountains or coasts. It has a written style, like travel guides, so in casual talk people say '신기하게 생긴 바위' (a strange-looking rock).

examples.en: Strange rocky cliffs stretched out along the river.
We took a boat and passed between the rocky cliffs.

examples.ko: 기암절벽의 꼭대기에 작은 정자가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A small pavilion stands at the top of the rocky cliff.
This place is famous for its rocky cliffs and clear water.
Looking at the rocky cliffs made my heart feel refreshed.
In autumn, the maple leaves turn beautifully colored on the rocky cliffs.

explain: '기암괴석'은 모양이 특이한 바위를, '기암절벽'은 그런 바위로 이루어진 벼랑을 말할 때 어울려요. 둘 다 풍경을 설명하는 글에서 잘 만나요.
explain_en: '기암괴석' fits oddly shaped rocks, while '기암절벽' fits a cliff made of such rocks. Both are common in descriptions of scenery.

examples.ko: 내일은 기압골의 영향으로 전국에 비가 와요.
examples.en: Tomorrow it will rain nationwide because of a pressure trough.
A pressure trough is approaching from the west.
Clouds spread widely along the pressure trough.

examples.ko: 일기예보에서 기압골 때문에 비가 온다고 했어요.
examples.en: The weather forecast said it will rain because of a pressure trough.

examples.ko: 기압골에 의해 제주도에 많은 눈이 내린대요.
examples.en: I heard heavy snow is falling on Jeju because of a pressure trough.
It thundered all night because of a pressure trough.

explain: 일기예보에서 '기압골의 영향으로 비가 오겠습니다'처럼 들리는 말이에요. 친구와 말할 때는 '비구름이 온대'처럼 쉽게 말해요.
explain_en: You hear it in weather forecasts, as in '기압골의 영향으로 비가 오겠습니다' (rain is expected due to a pressure trough). With friends, people say it simply, like '비구름이 온대' (rain clouds are coming).

examples.en: The owner of that company apologized to the employees.

examples.ko: 기업주는 올해 월급을 올려 주겠다고 약속했어요.
examples.en: The business owner promised to raise salaries this year.

examples.ko: 작은 가게 기업주도 요즘 많이 힘들다고 해요.
examples.en: Owners of small shops say it's very hard these days too.
The business owner and the workers began talking together.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 기업주를 만난 기자가 질문을 했어요.
examples.en: On the news, a reporter who met the business owner asked questions.

examples.ko: 이 공장의 기업주에게 직접 편지를 보냈어요.
examples.en: I sent a letter directly to the owner of this factory.

explain: '사장'은 회사에서 부르는 직책 이름이고, 뉴스나 글에서 회사의 주인을 가리킬 때 '기업주'라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 '사장님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '사장' is a job title used at a company, while news and writing use '기업주' for the owner of a company. When you address the person directly, say '사장님'.

examples.ko: 지붕 위의 기왓장이 바람에 몇 장 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: A few roof tiles fell off the roof in the wind.
I found a broken roof tile at the old temple.
Snow piled up softly on the roof tiles.
The roof of a hanok is covered with roof tiles.

examples.ko: 아이들이 기왓장에 이름을 써서 소원을 빌었어요.
examples.en: The children wrote their names on a roof tile and made a wish.
At an excavation site, even roof tiles are important material.

explain: 지붕 재료를 통틀어 말할 때는 '기와', 한 장 한 장을 말할 때는 '기왓장'이 자연스러워요. '기와'에 'ㅅ'이 들어간 모양으로 쓰고, '기와짱'으로 소리 나요.
explain_en: Use '기와' for the roofing material in general and '기왓장' when talking about individual tiles. It is written with an extra 'ㅅ' after '기와' and pronounced '기와짱'.

examples.ko: 탁자가 기우뚱 기울자 물병이 바닥에 쓰러졌어요.
examples.en: When the table tilted, the water bottle fell over onto the floor.
The boat rocked to one side, and I felt a little scared.
The child walked unsteadily and almost fell.

examples.ko: 강아지가 고개를 기우뚱 기울이고 저를 봐요.
examples.en: My puppy tilts its head and looks at me.

examples.ko: 의자 다리가 짧아서 앉으면 기우뚱 기울어요.
examples.en: One chair leg is short, so it tilts when you sit.

examples.ko: 버스가 급하게 돌자 사람들이 기우뚱 쏠렸어요.
examples.en: When the bus turned sharply, people lurched to one side.

explain: 물건이 한쪽으로 쏠려 곧 넘어질 듯한 모습을 그려요. '고개를 기우뚱'은 궁금하거나 이해가 안 될 때 하는 행동이에요. 더 작고 가벼운 느낌은 '갸우뚱'이에요.
explain_en: It paints a picture of something tilting to one side as if about to fall. '고개를 기우뚱' is what people do when curious or puzzled. '갸우뚱' feels smaller and lighter.

examples.en: The boat kept rocking in the waves, and I felt seasick.
The boxes stacked like a tower keep wobbling.
The baby is wobbling while taking first steps.
The desk was wobbling, so I put paper under it.
The bicycle wobbled and finally fell over.

examples.ko: 버스 안에서 사람들이 기우뚱거리며 서 있었어요.
examples.en: People were standing and swaying on the bus.

explain: 한 번 기우는 '기우뚱하다'와 달리 이쪽저쪽으로 계속 흔들릴 때 써요. '고개를 기우뚱거리다'처럼 쓸 수도 있고 '기우뚱대다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Unlike '기우뚱하다', which tilts once, this is for swaying or wobbling again and again. You can also say '고개를 기우뚱거리다' (to keep tilting one's head), and '기우뚱대다' is another form.

examples.ko: 탁자가 기우뚱하자 컵이 바닥에 떨어져 깨졌어요.
examples.en: When the table tilted, the cup fell to the floor and broke.
The boat tilted, so everyone slid to one side.

examples.ko: 그림이 기우뚱해 보이는데 좀 바로잡아 주세요.
examples.en: The picture looks crooked, so please straighten it.
Every time the chair tilts, I sit down carefully.
The child tilted her head and asked me.
The luggage shifted to one side, and the car leaned.

explain: '기울다'보다 균형이 깨질 듯 불안한 느낌이 있어요. '기우뚱한 탑'처럼 꾸미는 말로도 쓰고, '고개를 기우뚱하다'는 궁금해하는 모습이에요.
explain_en: It feels more unstable than '기울다', as if balance is about to break. You can use it to describe a noun, as in '기우뚱한 탑' (a leaning tower), and '고개를 기우뚱하다' shows someone wondering.

examples.ko: 그 지역은 비가 적어 해마다 기우제를 지냈어요.
examples.en: That region gets little rain, so they held a rain ritual every year.
After a long drought, a rain ritual was held.

examples.ko: 이 마을에는 기우제에 얽힌 이야기가 전해져요.
examples.en: This village has a story about a rain ritual passed down.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 옛 기우제의 모습을 영상으로 봤어요.
examples.en: At the museum, I watched a video of an old rain ritual.

examples.ko: 비가 안 오면 기우제까지 지낸다고 하더라고요.
examples.en: They say that if it doesn't rain, they even hold a rain ritual.

examples.ko: 그 마을은 기우제도 지내고 우물도 새로 팠어요.
examples.en: That village held a rain ritual and also dug a new well.

explain: 가뭄 때 비를 내려 달라고 빌던 제사예요. '기우제를 지내다'처럼 '지내다'와 같이 써요. 역사나 전통 이야기에서 자주 만나는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is the ritual people performed to pray for rain during a drought. It goes with '지내다', as in '기우제를 지내다'. You mostly meet it in stories about history and tradition.

examples.en: The school bought new equipment for experiments.

examples.ko: 행사 기자재는 전날 미리 옮겨 놓았어요.
examples.en: We moved the event equipment the day before.
This room is full of broadcasting equipment.
Please apply for equipment rental at the office.

examples.ko: 촬영 기자재도 함께 빌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also borrow the filming equipment together.
We learned how to use the new equipment.

explain: '장비'보다 딱딱한 글말이에요. 학교, 공사, 방송 현장에서 기계와 도구를 한꺼번에 묶어 부를 때 써요. 하나하나를 말할 때는 '카메라', '마이크'처럼 이름을 말해요.
explain_en: It is stiffer and more formal than '장비'. It bundles machines and tools together at schools, construction sites and broadcast sites. For individual items, people use names like '카메라' or '마이크'.

en: be frightened; be shocked; be astounded

examples.en: My younger sibling saw a cockroach in the room and freaked out.
I almost fainted from shock when I heard that price.

examples.ko: 갑자기 불이 꺼져서 다들 기절초풍하고 소리를 질렀어요.
examples.en: The lights suddenly went out, and everyone was terrified and screamed.

examples.ko: 시험 점수를 보면 엄마가 기절초풍하실 거예요.
examples.en: Mom will be shocked when she sees my test score.

examples.ko: 문을 열자 고양이가 튀어나와서 기절초풍하며 뒤로 물러났어요.
examples.en: A cat jumped out when I opened the door, and I was so startled that I stepped back.
My friend's shocked face was so funny.

explain: '놀라다', '깜짝 놀라다'보다 훨씬 크게 놀랐다고 과장해서 말하는 느낌이에요. 주로 무섭거나 어이없는 일에 쓰고, 말투가 가볍고 재미있어서 격식 있는 글에는 잘 안 맞아요.
explain_en: It exaggerates how much you were startled, much stronger than '놀라다' or '깜짝 놀라다'. It is mostly used for scary or absurd things, and the tone is light and playful, so it does not suit formal writing.

examples.ko: 그 회사가 문을 닫는 것은 이미 기정사실이에요.
examples.en: It's already a settled fact that the company is closing.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 사귄다는 소문이 기정사실처럼 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: The rumor that the two are dating spread as if it were a fact.
The mood is to accept the team's victory as a given.

examples.ko: 기정사실이 되어 버려서 이제 바꿀 수가 없어요.
examples.en: It has become a done deal, so we can't change it now.
I believed passing was certain, but I failed.

examples.ko: 이미 기정사실인 일을 두고 왜 싸워요?
examples.en: Why are you fighting over something that's already settled?

explain: 아직 공식 발표는 없어도 이미 정해진 일처럼 여겨질 때 써요. '~을 기정사실로 받아들이다/하다'처럼 자주 쓰고, '기정사실화하다'라는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: You use it for something treated as already settled, even before an official announcement. It often appears as '~을 기정사실로 받아들이다/하다', and there is also the verb '기정사실화하다'.

examples.en: I ran until I was completely worn out.
When the game ended, all the players were totally exhausted.
I came home with an exhausted face.
After the hike, I was so exhausted that I fell asleep right away.

examples.ko: 지금 기진맥진 직전이라서 한 걸음도 못 걷겠어요.
examples.en: I'm on the verge of collapse, so I can't take another step.
I went into the meeting in a totally exhausted state.

explain: '피곤하다'보다 훨씬 강하게, 힘이 완전히 빠져 움직이기도 힘든 상태를 말해요. 보통 '기진맥진했어요', '기진맥진 상태예요'처럼 써요. '녹초가 되다'도 비슷하게 말해요.
explain_en: It is much stronger than '피곤하다', describing a state where all your strength is gone and moving is hard. It is usually used as '기진맥진했어요' or '기진맥진 상태예요'. '녹초가 되다' is a similar expression.

en: be completely exhausted; be absolutely worn out

examples.en: I walked on mountain trails all day and I'm completely worn out.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나고 나니 기진맥진해서 말도 안 나와요.
examples.en: After the exam, I'm so exhausted I can't even speak.
The exhausted children fell asleep in the car.
I didn't know I would be this worn out.
After working all night, I'm always completely drained.
When I'm totally exhausted, I don't want to do anything.

explain: '피곤하다'나 '지치다'보다 힘이 완전히 빠진 상태를 강조해요. 달리기, 등산, 야근처럼 몸을 많이 쓴 뒤에 어울려요. '녹초가 되다'도 비슷해요.
explain_en: It stresses that all your strength is gone, stronger than '피곤하다' or '지치다'. It suits times after heavy physical effort such as running, hiking or overtime. '녹초가 되다' is similar.

examples.en: It seemed like I heard someone from somewhere.

examples.ko: 문 밖에서는 아무 기척도 느껴지지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't sense any sign of anyone outside the door.

examples.ko: 아기가 깰까 봐 기척을 내지 않고 나갔어요.
examples.en: I left without making a sound so the baby wouldn't wake up.
Startled by a sudden sound of someone, I looked behind me.

examples.ko: 그는 기척 없이 제 뒤에 서 있었어요.
examples.en: He was standing behind me without making a sound.
I only sensed that someone was there, but I couldn't see anyone.

explain: '기척이 나다/느껴지다', '기척을 내다'처럼 소리나 움직임으로 누가 있다는 낌새를 말해요. 사람이 있는 낌새는 '인기척'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the hint of someone's presence through sound or movement, as in '기척이 나다/느껴지다' and '기척을 내다'. A sign that a person is there is also called '인기척'.

examples.ko: 불편한 점이 있으면 기탄없이 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: If anything is inconvenient, please tell us frankly.
Let's share our opinions openly in the meeting.
You can ask the teacher questions without hesitating.

examples.ko: 친구들끼리 기탄없이 이야기하다 보니 밤이 깊었어요.
examples.en: We talked so freely among friends that it became late at night.

examples.ko: 제가 고칠 부분을 기탄없이 지적해 주세요.
examples.en: Please point out frankly what I should fix.
The two of them opened up about their true feelings without reserve.

explain: 꺼리거나 눈치 보지 않고 말한다는 느낌이라서 '기탄없이 말씀해 주세요'처럼 정중하게 의견을 청할 때 잘 써요. 친구끼리는 '편하게', '솔직하게'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It means speaking without holding back or worrying about others' reactions, so it fits polite requests like '기탄없이 말씀해 주세요'. Among friends, people say '편하게' or '솔직하게'.

examples.en: I stamped my ballot in the polling booth inside the polling station.

examples.ko: 기표소에는 한 사람씩만 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only one person at a time can enter the voting booth.

examples.ko: 기표소 안에서는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos inside the voting booth.
I waited in line and went into the voting booth.
I left the booth and put my ballot into the ballot box.

examples.ko: 기표소가 좁아서 휠체어는 들어가기 어려워 보였어요.
examples.en: The booth was narrow, so it looked hard for a wheelchair to get in.

explain: '투표소'는 투표하는 장소 전체고, '기표소'는 그 안에서 혼자 표시하는 칸막이 공간이에요. 선거 뉴스에서 만나는 말이에요.
explain_en: '투표소' is the whole place where voting takes place, while '기표소' is the partitioned space inside where you mark your ballot alone. You meet it in election news.

examples.ko: 최근 몇 년 사이에 인구가 기하급수적으로 늘었어요.
examples.en: The population has grown exponentially in the last few years.
The server stopped because of the exponential increase.
The rumor is spreading at nearly an exponential speed.

examples.ko: 기하급수적 증가를 막으려고 새 규칙을 만들었어요.
examples.en: We made a new rule to stop the exponential increase.
It increased so fast that you could call it exponential.
Sales rose so quickly it was almost exponential.

explain: 늘거나 줄어드는 속도가 점점 빨라질 때 써요. 뉴스에서는 '기하급수적으로 늘다/증가하다'로 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '엄청나게', '폭발적으로'가 더 편해요. '기하급수적인', '기하급수적으로'처럼 활용해서 써요.
explain_en: You use it when an increase or decrease keeps speeding up. News often says '기하급수적으로 늘다/증가하다', while in daily talk '엄청나게' or '폭발적으로' feels easier. It appears in forms such as '기하급수적인' and '기하급수적으로'.

examples.ko: 선수가 기합을 넣고 공을 힘껏 찼어요.
examples.en: The player let out a shout and kicked the ball with all his might.

examples.ko: 도장에서 큰 기합 소리가 울려 퍼졌어요.
examples.en: A loud shout echoed through the training hall.
I answered in a voice full of energy and spirit.
The baby burst into tears, startled by the shout.
He threw his opponent with a shout.
I heard there was a time when people were punished with hard physical drills.

explain: 운동이나 무술에서 힘을 모으려고 내는 소리를 말하고, '기합을 넣다'처럼 정신을 바짝 차리게 하는 말로도 써요. '기합을 받다'는 벌로 힘든 동작을 하는 것을 말해요.
explain_en: It is the shout made to gather strength in sports or martial arts, and '기합을 넣다' also means to get your spirit sharp and focused. '기합을 받다' means to be made to do hard physical drills as punishment.
